history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2306 is a confirmed duplicate of seq 1011 (id jogulamba-temple-alampur-jogulamba-gadwal) - keep/drop decision needed for the CSV row. The Alampur Jogulamba Temple is one of the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas (the fifth of the Ashtadasa peethas), the spot where Sati Devi's upper teeth are believed to have fallen. The original shrine was built in the 7th century CE under the Badami Chalukyas within the Navabrahma temple complex (nine Chalukyan Shiva temples). It was destroyed by the Bahmani Sultans in 1390 CE; the idol was hidden in the nearby Bala Brahma temple and worshipped there in secret for over 600 years. The temple was rebuilt at its former location and reconsecrated in 2005. In 2019 it was included under the Government of India PRASAD scheme.
